obligations.note: The new compatibility route GET /compat/account-number/{id} returns a Route with mfa=False for the action view_account_number, which is listed as a privileged action in controls/payments/access-policy.json. The _authenticate method gates MFA on route.mfa, so this path allows a privileged action without multi-factor authentication. Additionally, the route is dispatched before the ROUTE_TABLE loop, serving a route outside the approved route table, violating the 'no route is served outside the route table' clause.
Ticket CHG-26510 is approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) and lists component payments.http, which per components.json covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/app.py, the only file changed.
Sofia Santos (payments-eng, change_approver for payments) submitted a code_review approval on the head commit; she is not the author (Mara Costa).
The sole commit 74fd9836 is the one named in both approvals; no later commits exist to void the approval.

CI run.json shows the run on the head commit 74fd9836 with 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; all registered control tests including test_privileged_routes_require_mfa are present and passing.
app.py belongs to component payments.http which is security_sensitive; Ines Halvorsen (platform-security, security_reviewer) approved with kind security_review on the head commit.
The change does not touch any protected path (controls/, test controls, ci/); no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket is of type standard, not emergency; no post-implementation review is triggered.

The MFA-1 violation is a deviation from a product obligation, but the exception register contains no approved, unexpired, in-scope exception for MFA-1 on payments (EXC-0172 is for mortgage.routes and is withdrawn); the deviation is unauthorised.

summary: The change adds a compatibility URL /compat/account-number/{id} in the match() function of app.py that returns a Route with mfa=False for the privileged action view_account_number, bypassing the multi-factor authentication requirement and serving the route outside the approved route table. This directly violates MFA-1 and, because no valid exception in the register covers this deviation, also violates EXC-1. All other applicable obligations (change ticket, independent approval, approval coverage, CI testing, security review, non-protected paths, non-emergency) are satisfied. The change must be rejected until the MFA bypass is removed or a properly scoped, approved exception with a compensating control is recorded.
